required_tuples.rationale: POST /api/users with only username and password creates an inactive account of type user with the default user permissions, no email, empty lists and a bcrypt password hash, and answers {user} in the browser view.

POST /api/users with type admin, email, isActive, permission overrides and library and tag selections (top-level or inside permissions) stores them in the permissions JSON; the new account logs in, is listed and read back by id.
POST /api/users keeps the type's defaults for permission keys the server does not know and stores no such key in users.permissions.

POST /api/users with the account modal's full permissions object stores each of the nine flags set to the opposite of its type default, for user, admin and guest, in the response and in users.permissions.
POST /api/users keeps an empty-string email as the empty string, stores a null email as NULL, and stores empty top-level librariesAccessible and itemTagsSelected as empty lists.
A non-root admin may create users of every type except root, admins included; type root is rejected with 400.
The username uniqueness check compares the exact text: a name differing only in case is accepted as a different user, and a Unicode name is stored and can log in.
POST /api/users answers 400 for a missing, empty or non-string username or password, an unknown account type and a taken username, and changes no row.
Posting the same new username twice creates it once: the second request answers 400 and the first account keeps its row and password.
POST /api/users answers 401 without a valid token and 403 to non-admin users, and creates nothing.
Creating a user emits user_added with the new user's browser view (equal to the response) to every admin socket, root and non-root, and not to a non-admin user's socket.
Each created user emits its own user_added event, in creation order, also when a non-root admin does the creating, and the creating admin receives it too.
After a user is renamed, creating a user with the freed name succeeds and emits user_added for the new account.
A rejected create (duplicate username, invalid body, forbidden caller) emits no user_added event to any socket.

DELETE /api/users/:id answers {success:true} and removes the user row with its progress, auth sessions, playlists (and their items), devices and API keys, keeps its playback sessions, RSS feeds, shares and the API keys it created with a null user id, revokes its access token and login, and leaves other users' data.
DELETE /api/users/:id on a fresh user without any data answers {success:true}, removes exactly that row and leaves every other user row untouched.
A non-root admin may delete a user, including an admin; deleting the same id again answers 404.
DELETE /api/users/:id answers 401 unauthenticated, 403 to non-admins and to an admin targeting root, 400 when an admin targets itself (root included), 404 for an unknown id, and removes nothing.
Deleting a user emits user_removed with the deleted user's browser view (id, username, type, token, permissions) to every admin socket and not to an ordinary user's socket.
The user_removed payload of a user with progress and bookmarks carries them (mediaProgress and bookmarks arrays), and the deleted user's own connected socket receives no user_removed.
Deleting a user emits user_removed once; deleting the same id again answers 404 and emits nothing more.
A rejected delete (self, root, unknown id, forbidden caller) emits no user_removed event.
GET /api/users/:id as root returns the full browser view of the listener with its seven media progress entries (display title, subtitle, cover path and media update time added) and its two bookmarks.
GET /api/users/:id of the root user shows its token to root and an empty string to another admin, and a user without progress or bookmarks gets empty arrays.
GET /api/users/:id answers 401 without a valid token, 403 to a non-admin for any id including its own, and 404 for an unknown id to an admin.
GET /api/users as root returns every user in the minimal browser view: identity, type, token, flags, permissions and selection lists, without mediaProgress and bookmarks.
GET /api/users as a non-root admin shows the root user's token as an empty string and every other user's token unchanged.
GET /api/users?include=latestSession adds each user's most recently updated playback session or null; the include list is comma separated and trimmed; without it the key is absent.
GET /api/users answers 401 without a valid token and 403 to a non-admin user.
GET /api/users/:id/listening-sessions as root returns the user's seven playback sessions newest update first, each with the target user's id and username, and the paging envelope.
itemsPerPage and page slice the sessions and numPages rounds up; a page beyond the end is an empty array; a user without sessions has total 0 and numPages 0.
GET /api/users/:id/listening-sessions answers 401 without a valid token, 404 for an unknown id to an admin, and to a non-admin 403 for any other user's id but 200 for its own id.
GET /api/users/:id/listening-stats as root sums the listener's sessions: totalTime, per-item time and metadata, per-date and per-weekday time, today 0 and the ten most recent sessions.
A user without sessions has zero stats and empty objects; after the user listens for five seconds today's time, the date, the weekday and the item time each show five.
GET /api/users/:id/listening-stats answers 401 without a valid token, 404 for an unknown id to an admin, and to a non-admin 403 for any other user's id but 200 for its own id.
GET /api/users/online lists each user with an authenticated socket once with the public user fields and the number of connections, and omits users without a socket.
A user with an open playback session shows that session in usersOnline and openSessions, and leaves usersOnline when the last socket disconnects.
GET /api/users/online answers 401 without a valid token and 403 to a non-admin user, and 200 to a non-root admin.

PATCH /api/users/:id/openid-unlink on a linked user answers 200, sets extraData.authOpenIDSub to null keeping the other extraData, changes no other column but the update time, and emits user_updated with hasOpenIDLink false to the acting admin only.
Unlinking a user that has no OpenID link, including a second unlink, answers 200 and changes nothing and emits no event; root's own record may be targeted by any admin the same way.
A non-root admin may unlink a user; the event goes to that admin's sockets and the link is gone for later reads.
PATCH openid-unlink answers 401 unauthenticated, 403 to non-admins (also for their own id) and 404 for an unknown id, leaving a linked user linked and emitting no event.

PATCH /api/users/:id changes email, type, isActive and the permission flags and selection lists, answers {success, user} and stores them, leaving username, password hash, token and creation time as they were.
PATCH librariesAccessible or itemTagsSelected at the top level changes nothing unless a permissions object is sent too; with one they are applied, and empty arrays (truthy) clear them.
PATCH skips unknown permission keys, non-boolean permission values, malformed lists, an empty password, an empty email and an unchanged type while applying the valid parts of the same request.
Sending the same PATCH again answers success with the same user and writes nothing (the row, including its update time, is unchanged) and emits no user_updated event.

PATCH password stores a new bcrypt hash, makes the old password fail and the new one log in, deletes the user's auth sessions so the old refresh token stops working, and leaves the stored api token as it was.
An admin changing its own password while presenting its refresh token keeps that one auth session (rotated, still refreshable) and loses its other sessions, while the old password stops working.

PATCH username renames the user, issues a new stored api token, deletes its auth sessions, and the user logs in under the new name only; a taken name is rejected with 400 and nothing changes; sending the current name changes nothing.
PATCH isActive false makes login, API calls with an existing access token and socket authentication fail; PATCH isActive true restores them.
Root may edit itself but its type cannot change (the type key is ignored); a non-root admin editing the root user gets 403, while an admin may edit other users and promote a user to admin.

PATCH with the account modal's body (full permissions object plus top-level lists) flips each of the nine flags away from the type default and then back, for user, admin and guest, in the response and in users.permissions.

PATCH may rename a user to a case variant of its own or another name (the check is exact), and username with password in one request makes one new token, deletes the auth sessions, emits one user_updated, and logs in under the new name and password only.

PATCH /api/users/:id answers 401 unauthenticated, 403 to non-admins (also for their own id), 404 for an unknown id, and 400 for id, pash, token, extraData or bookmarks keys, a non-string email or username, an unknown or root type and non-object permissions, changing no row.

A PATCH that changes a user emits user_updated with the updated browser view (equal to the response) to the sockets of the admin who made the request only: not to the edited user, another admin or an ordinary user.
When a non-root admin edits a user, that admin's socket receives user_updated and root's does not; a PATCH of a user's own record by an admin also reaches the admin's sockets.
Each PATCH that changes something emits its own user_updated carrying the then-current value; repeating the last PATCH emits nothing.
A rejected PATCH and a PATCH that changes nothing emit no user_updated event.
